definition.message:
{{#is_alert}}
## What's happening?

Firewall **{{@device_hostname.name}}** logged an HA state change in the last 5 minutes.
{{/is_alert}}

{{^is_recovery}}

---

## Impact

If this is a failover, traffic moved to the peer firewall. Sessions that were not synchronized may have been dropped.

---

## Why?

Possible causes:
* **A link or path monitoring failure** on the previously active firewall.
* **A device failure or reboot.**
* **A manual failover or suspend.**

---

## How to troubleshoot and resolve the issue?

1. Check the log sample for the old and new HA state.
2. Run `show high-availability all` on both peers to confirm their current state.
3. If this is a failover, find out why the previously active peer gave up the role, and whether it is healthy.

---

## Related links

* [Documentation](https://docs.datadoghq.com/integrations/pan_firewall/)
* [Logs](/logs?query=source:pan.firewall+@type:SYSTEM+@subtype:ha+@device_hostname:{{@device_hostname.name}})
{{/is_recovery}}
definition.name: [Palo Alto Networks Firewall] HA state changed on {{@device_hostname.name}}

description: Alerts when a firewall logs an HA state change (system log, subtype `ha`, event `state-change`), such as a failover. Both peers log it, so a failover alerts once per firewall. A reboot or a suspended unit also alerts. Requires Palo Alto Networks Firewall log collection.
title: HA state changed
